findings.description: The newcomer's kickoff still lists every peer from `scopeConflicts`, including peers that share only `docs/09-decisions.md` and peers that are not running. The session protocol then tells the newcomer to message each one before editing a shared file. So the newcomer's own SendMessage wakes the idle peer that `introduceToPeers` now skips. "An overlap on this log alone wakes no one" does not hold, and the awaiting-review/blocked saving shrinks by the same amount.
findings.body:
Decision 104 stops pup from waking a peer that shares only the decisions log, or one that is not `running`. But the newcomer's kickoff still names those peers, and the protocol tells it to contact them first.

The kickoff receives the unfiltered conflicts. `filesWorthANotice` and the `state !== 'running'` check only run inside `introduceToPeers`:

```ts
const sessionId = startSession(db, { ...req, task }, route, conflicts.map(peerOf));
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3ae7a163cf43d862c2176157537fd309f0cefd2e/src/core/session-lifecycle.service.ts#L214-L214

```ts
function peerOf(conflict: ScopeConflict): SessionPeer {
  return { name: windowLabel({ sessionId: conflict.sessionId }), files: conflict.files };
}
```
https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3ae7a163cf43d862c2176157537fd309f0cefd2e/src/core/session-lifecycle.service.ts#L239-L241

Every kickoff's protocol says:

> Peer sessions may share your files: those under Peers above ... Before editing a shared file, message the peer what you will change

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/3ae7a163cf43d862c2176157537fd309f0cefd2e/src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts#L313-L318

Any `docs/**` scope includes `docs/09-decisions.md`, so a newcomer with such a scope will SendMessage a log-only peer before it appends its decision. An idle or awaiting-review peer is woken by that message, which is the cost this decision measured and set out to avoid (decision 47: a message "queues until the current tool call ends"). The new test `sends no introduction for an overlap on the append-only decisions log alone` asserts that the kickoff still contains ``- `pup-s-docs` shares: docs/09-decisions.md``. Decision 104's reason for keeping the listing ("the newcomer is starting anyway") covers the newcomer's own cost. It does not cover the wake that the instructed message causes.

Possible fixes:
- (a) Pass `filesWorthANotice`-filtered peers into the kickoff and drop peers left with no files, while `scope_overlap` keeps the full record.
- (b) Keep the listing, but have the protocol say that the append-only log needs no message.

The same question applies, more weakly, to non-running peers listed under `## Peers`.

findings.description: Decision 104 says "A rejected or unblocked session resumes on a steer of its own and is gated again". But neither the gate-rejection resteer (`merge-gate.service.ts` ~L1942) nor `pup unblock` re-runs `recordOverlaps`. So a peer launched while a session was awaiting review or blocked is never introduced to it, and the record should call this an accepted gap rather than covered.

An awaiting-review or blocked session with an open PR no longer gets a main-landed notice telling it to `git merge` the target. It now takes in an overlapping land at the gate's fresh-base `git rebase` plus force-with-lease push. That rewrites PR history and can drop merge commits from earlier notices, a difference decision 104's "covered by fresh-base" claim does not mention.

`introduceToPeers` re-reads each peer with `getSession(...)?.state !== 'running'` inside the loop, while `steerOverlappingSessions` filters with `listSessions(db, ['running'])`. The same running-only rule now lives in two different shapes, with one extra query per conflict.

In the `introduceToPeers` JSDoc, "a fix round's own introduction reach it" is ambiguous. What reaches a skipped peer is the `## Peers` section of its own fix-round kickoff, not an introduction steer, which goes only to running peers. Suggested wording: "its own fix-round kickoff, which names every live peer".

Decision 99 still says "each peer is steered exactly once" and "it steers every live session whose branch changed a file the landed PR changed", but has no forward pointer to decision 104, which amends it. Add an "(amended by 104)" marker, following the existing "(amended 2026-10-18)" convention.

One line of decision 104 ("…the session with the conflict (decision 8), so a land it missed reaches it there. A session handed back by `pup fix`") runs about 118 columns. The surrounding decisions wrap near 100, so reflow it.
